summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplantation for cryptogenic cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and a pancreatic cyst was admitted for one week of epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, worsened by eating, and associated with nausea. Initial evaluation revealed elevated lipase and CT findings of peripancreatic fat stranding, confirming acute pancreatitis. The patient was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control using tramadol. His Bactrim was held due to its potential role in triggering pancreatitis. Renal function improved with hydration, and he advanced to a full diet as symptoms resolved. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid Bactrim and follow up with his transplant team for alternative prophylaxis.
